objective:
Create a new pure-Kotlin package com.mcfrenchpants.activityledger.core.domain.stats in core-domain (no Android, no I/O) holding the Explore screen's filter model and ALL of its counting rules, with exhaustive JVM tests. Read first for style and existing types: core-domain/.../model/TimePrecision.kt (EXACT, APPROXIMATE, DATE_ONLY, INFERRED_NOW), core-domain/.../lookup/HistoryLookup.kt (LookupEntry, KDoc style), core-domain/.../tagging/TagResolver.kt (how names/aliases are normalised; reuse its normalisation helper for case-insensitive matching if one exists, otherwise lowercase(Locale.ROOT)+trim), AGENTS.md.

Types to create (names are binding; later tasks depend on them):

1. ExploreEntry(occurrenceId: String, occurredAt: Instant, timePrecision: TimePrecision, durationSeconds: Long?, activityId: String, activityName: String, subjectId: String?, subjectName: String?, actionId: String?, actionName: String?, rawText: String?, subjectAliases: List<String> = emptyList(), actionAliases: List<String> = emptyList()). activityId/activityName are the canonical activity (always present); subject/action are null on old untagged rows. Only ACTIVE (accepted, visible) occurrences are ever passed in; the calculator does not filter visibility.

2. DateRangeSelection (sealed): Preset(kind: DateRangePreset { LAST_7_DAYS, LAST_30_DAYS, LAST_12_MONTHS, ALL_TIME }), Custom(start: LocalDate, endInclusive: LocalDate, label: RangeLabel? = null) where RangeLabel is sealed Month(YearMonth) | Year(Int) (used later when a question names a month or a year; UI words come later). Function resolve(selection, today: LocalDate, earliestEntryDate: LocalDate?): ResolvedRange(start: LocalDate, endInclusive: LocalDate, dayCount: Long) -- presets include today (LAST_30_DAYS = today and the 29 days before; LAST_7_DAYS = today + 6 before; LAST_12_MONTHS = today.minusMonths(12).plusDays(1)..today; ALL_TIME = earliestEntryDate (or today if none)..today). Custom bounds inclusive; reject start > end with require.

3. ExploreFilter(range: DateRangeSelection = Preset(LAST_30_DAYS), subjectId: String? = null, actionId: String? = null, words: String? = null) with isDefault.

4. ScopeKind { MANY, ONE_SUBJECT, ONE_ACTION, ONE_ACTIVITY } decided from the filter: subject+action set -> ONE_ACTIVITY; subject only -> ONE_SUBJECT; action only -> ONE_ACTION; else MANY (words alone -> MANY).

5. ExploreCalculator.calculate(entries: List<ExploreEntry>, filter: ExploreFilter, zone: ZoneId, now: Instant, firstDayOfWeek: DayOfWeek, activitySort: ActivitySort = MOST_LOGGED, entrySort: EntrySort = NEWEST, groupBySubject: Boolean = false): ExploreSummary. Pure and deterministic (stable tie-breaks: by occurredAt then occurrenceId; names case-insensitive then id).

Rules (from the approved design):
- Matching: tag filter matches subjectId/actionId equality (an untagged row never matches a tag filter). Word filter: case-insensitive substring of the trimmed words over rawText, activityName, subjectName, actionName, subjectAliases and actionAliases; blank words = no word filter. 'In scope (all time)' = tag+word filters only; 'in period' = in scope AND the local date of occurredAt (in zone) within the resolved range.
- Group by OCCURRED time in zone; day boundary local midnight; weeks start on firstDayOfWeek.
- ExploreSummary fields: scopeKind; range: ResolvedRange; totalEntriesEver: Int (all entries passed in, ignoring filters, so the UI can tell 'nothing logged at all' from 'nothing for these filters'); entriesInPeriod: Int; previousPeriodEntries: Int? = count in scope over the same-length period immediately before (start - dayCount .. start - 1), null for ALL_TIME and for ranges longer than 366 days; daysWithEntry: Int (distinct local dates in period); distinctActivities, distinctSubjects, distinctActions: Int (in period; untagged rows count as their own activity by activityId; distinctSubjects/Actions ignore null); lastTime: Instant? = newest occurredAt in scope over ALL TIME (not only in period); typicalGap: TypicalGap? (only meaningful for ONE_ACTIVITY; computed for the activity scope over all time, null if fewer than 3 entries or scope is not ONE_ACTIVITY); chart: ChartSeries; activities: List<ActivityRow>; subjectGroups: List<SubjectGroup>; patterns: Patterns; entries: List<ExploreEntry> (in period, sorted by entrySort NEWEST/OLDEST).
- Typical gap: for one activity (same subjectId+actionId, or same activityId for untagged rows), all-time entries sorted by time, consecutive gaps, median (even count -> mean of the two middle gaps); needs >=3 entries (>=2 gaps), else null. TypicalGap(duration: java.time.Duration, unit: GapUnit { HOURS, DAYS, MONTHS, YEARS }, amount: Long) with display rounding: < 2 days -> HOURS (rounded, min 1); < 60 days -> DAYS (rounded half up); < 2 years (730 days) -> MONTHS (days / 30.44 rounded); else YEARS (days / 365.25 rounded). Also expose isEveryDay (DAYS,1) and isEveryWeek (DAYS,7) helpers.
- ChartSeries(bucketSize: BucketSize { DAY, WEEK, MONTH }, buckets: List<ChartBucket(start: LocalDate, count: Int)>, average: Double? = mean count over buckets with count>0, null if none). DAY when range dayCount <= 31; WEEK when <= 371; else MONTH. Buckets cover the whole range with zeros included; WEEK buckets start on firstDayOfWeek (first bucket may begin before range start, still labelled by its week start; only count in-period entries); MONTH buckets start on the 1st.
- ActivityRow(activityId, activityName, subjectId?, subjectName?, actionId?, actionName?, countInPeriod: Int, lastTime: Instant (all time), typicalGap: TypicalGap? (all time, >=3 entries), entriesAllTime: Int). Only activities with countInPeriod >= 1. Sorts ActivitySort { MOST_LOGGED (count desc), LAST_DONE (lastTime desc), LONGEST_SINCE (lastTime asc), NAME (display name = 'subject · action' if tagged else activityName, case-insensitive) }. groupBySubject=true -> fill subjectGroups: List<SubjectGroup(subjectId?, subjectName (or activityName for untagged), countInPeriod, kinds: Int = distinct activities, lastTime)> sorted by the same sort semantics (empty list when groupBySubject=false).
- Patterns(byWeekday: List<Pair<DayOfWeek, Int>> 7 items starting at firstDayOfWeek; byPartOfDay: Map<PartOfDay, Int> with PartOfDay { MORNING 05:00-11:59, AFTERNOON 12:00-16:59, EVENING 17:00-21:59, NIGHT 22:00-04:59 } all keys present; partOfDayLeftOut: Int = in-period entries with DATE_ONLY precision; timeMentioned: List<TimeMentionedRow(activityId, activityName, subjectName?, actionName?, totalSeconds: Long, entryCount: Int)> over in-period entries with durationSeconds != null, sorted by totalSeconds desc; timeMentionedLeftOut: Int = in-period entries without a duration). Weekday counts include DATE_ONLY entries.

Tests in core-domain/src/test/kotlin/.../core/domain/stats/: fixed clock and zone (use America/Toronto or similar with DST), DST spring-forward and fall-back days (entry at 01:30 on fall-back day counted once, on the right date), entries at 23:59/00:00 local around range edges, presets include today, custom inclusive bounds, ALL_TIME starts at earliest entry, day-only precision in weekday but excluded from part of day with leftOut count, untagged rows (count as own activity; never match tag filters; grouped by activityName in subject roll-up), median with odd and even gap counts, fewer than 3 entries -> null gap, each rounding unit boundary (47h -> HOURS, 2 days -> DAYS, 59 vs 60 days, 729 vs 730 days), previous-period counts and null cases (ALL_TIME, >366 days), every scope kind, lastTime uses all time even when outside period, every activity sort and entry sort with tie-breaks, groupBySubject, word search over raw text / names / aliases case-insensitively, bucket size thresholds (31/32 days, 371/372) and week buckets honouring firstDayOfWeek (MONDAY and SUNDAY), average over non-empty buckets.

Do not change any existing file except where compilation strictly forces it (it should not). Add a short KDoc header on the package's main file pointing to the Explore design (docs/proposals/explore/DESIGN_SPEC.md 'Counting rules').
non_goals: No UI, no strings, no app-phone change.
No change to LookupService, HistoryLookup or TemporalResolver.
No wording/localisation: return structured values only.
acceptance_criteria: Package core.domain.stats exists with ExploreEntry, DateRangeSelection (+DateRangePreset, RangeLabel, ResolvedRange, resolve), ExploreFilter, ScopeKind, ExploreCalculator, ExploreSummary, TypicalGap/GapUnit, ChartSeries/ChartBucket/BucketSize, ActivityRow, SubjectGroup, ActivitySort, EntrySort, Patterns, PartOfDay, TimeMentionedRow with the fields named in the objective.

Every counting rule in the objective is implemented: occurred-time grouping in the given zone, inclusive presets/custom ranges, scope kinds, previous period (null for ALL_TIME and >366 days), daysWithEntry, distinct counts, lastTime over all time, typical gap median over all time with >=3 entries and the stated rounding units, bucket sizes and week starts, activity rows/sorts/grouping, patterns with left-out counts, word search over raw text/names/aliases.
The calculator is pure and deterministic with stable tie-breaks; no Android, I/O, logging or clock reads (now/zone/firstDayOfWeek are parameters).
JVM tests cover every item in the objective's test list and pass; ./gradlew :core-domain:test passes in full.
No file outside the stats main/test packages is changed.
